# Tagcast 1.9.5

Tagcast 1.9.5 adds **Discover similar music**, supports both iBroadcast multi-disc
display settings, and makes metadata suggestions less cluttered.

## Discover albums already in your library

- Open an album artist and choose **Discover similar music**. Tagcast shows up to
  six albums by other artists in your loaded iBroadcast library.
- Last.fm is the default. It supplies related artists, which Tagcast matches
  against your library. Album ratings help choose an album for each artist.
  Enable Last.fm and add an API key under **Settings → Sources & keys**; no Last.fm
  user login or listening history is needed.
- When a successful Last.fm search has no usable local matches, Tagcast shows
  clearly labelled suggestions based on shared genres. Missing keys, unavailable
  services and other errors are reported separately.
- To use local genres only, turn off **Use Last.fm for similar artists** under
  **Settings → Discovery** and save. The choice is remembered across restarts.
- Searching starts only after Discover or Refresh. Last.fm receives the chosen
  artist name and API key, without library records, iBroadcast credentials,
  listening history or audio. The privacy explanation is in Settings and Help.
- Open, Play and Queue use the existing album controls. Opening a suggestion
  labels its breadcrumb **Discover from [artist]**; returning restores the
  artist page, suggestions, filters and scroll position.

## Both iBroadcast multi-disc display settings

Tagcast can now read libraries with **Combine Multi-Disc Album Sets** either on
or off. Recognized combined track lists are shown with disc headings and readable
track numbers, while the original IDs and native positions remain unchanged.

With combining on, supported track fields can still be edited through the normal
review and save process. Album information, track-number edits, album splitting,
merging and album-artist cleanup remain restricted. Missing original disc IDs or
album fields are not reconstructed.

For full album editing, turn combining off in iBroadcast and reload Tagcast.
Tagcast can still group those separate discs visually as one set. A dismissible
banner and a short explanation under **Settings → Interface** describe the
recommendation. Tagcast never changes the iBroadcast preference itself.

See [iBroadcast multi-disc views](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/main/docs/combined-albums.md)
for the supported shapes and remaining restrictions.

## Quieter metadata suggestions

Sources that finish without a match no longer leave large empty blocks in the
metadata editor. Matches stay visible, along with loading states, errors and
missing-key guidance. If every requested source is empty, one compact **No match**
message appears. Suggestions still fill the editor; saving still requires review.

## Updating and documentation

- From 1.9.0, supported signed macOS apps and installed Debian/Ubuntu copies can
  download an update in Tagcast and install it after confirmation. Homebrew copies
  keep the Homebrew update route. Unsigned Windows, portable archives and source
  installations keep their manual update routes.
- Users on 1.8.0 or older should install 1.9.5 through the normal download or
  package-manager route. Settings and sign-in data remain in their normal folders.
- macOS downloads cover Apple Silicon and Intel and use Developer ID signing and
  Apple notarization. Windows downloads remain unsigned. Every application
  package has a SHA-256 companion.
- The [illustrated PDF manual](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/PDF-manual)
  remains the 1.9.0 edition. These release notes and the repository's
  [Discover guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/main/docs/discover.md)
  describe the new controls.

Tagcast remains an independent app for iBroadcast. Existing local music files
are never retagged; explicit audio downloads create separate copies. Gapless
playback remains experimental, optional and off by default.
